title: Polyphenol extract ameliorates diabetes-related atherosclerosis through HIF-1 signaling pathway in APOE(-/)(-) mice: Possible synergism with atorvastatin.
authors: Yang, Yang; Chen, Shengxiang; Shi, Guanjin; Huang, Shanshan; Cui, Ningning; Tan, Le; Yang, Xuefeng
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究多酚提取物改善糖尿病动脉粥样硬化的机制，涉及HIF-1信号通路，但核心是疾病表型与信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、TF-DNA结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus promotes atherosclerosis (AS), a major cause of cardiovascular disease. Statins, clinical drugs for AS treatment, may increase the risk of diabetes and induce hepatotoxicity. Polyphenols can alleviate AS by exerting anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, and play a role in liver protection. However, the effects of polyphenol extract (PE) on diabetic AS and whether PE can assist atorvastatin in managing diabetic AS with additional benefits remain poorly understood. PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the synergistic effects of a type of PE with atorvastatin on diabetic AS, as well as explore the anti-atherogenic mechanisms of PE. METHODS: Polyphenol constituents in PE were identified using UPLC-MS/MS. Streptozocin -induced diabetic ApoE(-/)(-) mice were orally administered 350 and 700 mg/kg of PE, 10 mg/kg of atorvastatin, or 5 mg/kg of atorvastatin+700 mg/kg of PE for 10 weeks. Atherosclerotic lesions and plaque stability were evaluated using Oil Red O staining, Sirius red staining, and immunofluorescence. Inflammation and oxidative stress were determined using the corresponding markers. Hepatic pathological changes were assessed using hematoxylin and eosin staining. Network pharmacology prediction, molecular docking, microscale thermophoresis (MST) and western blotting were used to explore the anti-atherosclerotic mechanisms of PE. RESULTS: The polyphenolic constituents of PE mainly consist of flavonoids and phenolic acids. PE treatment effectively mitigated atherosclerotic lesions in diabetic mice, particularly at high dose. Co-treatment with a half-dose of atorvastatin and PE did not restrain the anti-atherosclerotic effects of atorvastatin treatment, whereas the combination better relieved hyperglycemia, inflammation, oxidative stress, and liver damage in diabetic AS compared to that with atorvastatin alone. In addition, network pharmacology, molecular docking, MST and western blotting results indicated that PE ameliorated diabetic AS, possibly by targeting the AKT/mTOR/HIF-1 signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: The PE demonstrated efficacy against diabetic AS and cooperated with atorvastatin for some additional benefits, especially in liver protection, indicating that PE has the potential to be developed as a supplement for the management of diabetes-related AS.
abstract_zh: 背景：糖尿病促进动脉粥样硬化（AS），这是心血管疾病的主要原因。他汀类药物作为AS的临床治疗药物，可能增加糖尿病风险并诱发肝毒性。多酚通过发挥抗炎和抗氧化作用可缓解AS，并在肝脏保护中发挥作用。然而，多酚提取物（PE）对糖尿病AS的影响以及PE是否能辅助阿托伐他汀管理糖尿病AS并带来额外益处，仍知之甚少。目的：本研究旨在探讨一种多酚提取物与阿托伐他汀对糖尿病AS的协同作用，并探索PE的抗动脉粥样硬化机制。方法：采用UPLC-MS/MS鉴定PE中的多酚成分。链脲佐菌素诱导的糖尿病ApoE(-/-)小鼠分别口服350和700 mg/kg的PE、10 mg/kg的阿托伐他汀，或5 mg/kg的阿托伐他汀+700 mg/kg的PE，持续10周。使用油红O染色、天狼星红染色和免疫荧光评估动脉粥样硬化病变和斑块稳定性。通过相应标志物测定炎症和氧化应激。使用苏木精和伊红染色评估肝脏病理变化。采用网络药理学预测、分子对接、微量热泳动（MST）和蛋白质印迹法探索PE的抗动脉粥样硬化机制。结果：PE的多酚成分主要包括黄酮类和酚酸类。PE治疗有效减轻了糖尿病小鼠的动脉粥样硬化病变，尤其在高剂量下效果显著。半剂量阿托伐他汀与PE联合治疗并未抑制阿托伐他汀的抗动脉粥样硬化效果，而与单独使用阿托伐他汀相比，联合治疗更好地缓解了糖尿病AS中的高血糖、炎症、氧化应激和肝损伤。此外，网络药理学、分子对接、MST和蛋白质印迹结果表明，PE可能通过靶向AKT/mTOR/HIF-1信号通路改善糖尿病AS。结论：PE对糖尿病AS显示出疗效，并与阿托伐他汀协同带来一些额外益处，尤其在肝脏保护方面，表明PE有潜力被开发为管理糖尿病相关AS的补充剂。
